name: zquorum
title: zQuorum · anonymous quorums in Cairo
description: A group reaches a quorum without revealing who voted. Members register Pedersen commitments; a vote reveals only a nullifier — unlinkable to any member without their secret, and a repeated nullifier is a rejected double vote. All cryptography (commit, nullifier, set root, vote check) runs as a Cairo 2 program in circuit/ so the anchor never reimplements a hash, and the statement is already prover-shaped for the v0.2 STARK upgrade. Python-stdlib anchor keeps the quorum ledger (public books: tallies and nullifiers, never identities) over scarb 2.8.4.

protocol.scheme: commit/nullifier (Semaphore-style), Pedersen over the STARK field
protocol.root: fold pedersen('zq-root', ...) over the sorted commitment set
protocol.freeze: the member set freezes at the first vote
protocol.circuit: circuit/ (Cairo package zq); run via scarb cairo-run, tested via scarb cairo-test
protocol.trust_v0_1: anchor = trusted tallier; sees a secret transiently during verification, persists only (nullifier, choice)
protocol.upgrade_v0_2: STARK-prove the same circuit so votes verify without the tallier seeing secrets

state: data/quorums.json (gitignored runtime ledger). Secrets are never stored anywhere.

endpoints.POST /zquorum/commit: Derive a commitment from a secret (run client-side; secret=)
endpoints.POST /zquorum/vote: Cast an anonymous vote (name=, secret=, choice=yes|no)

safety: No chain, no keys, no funds: a local ceremony ledger. Secrets are verified by executing the Cairo circuit and are never persisted; the ledger stores commitments, nullifiers and choices only. route=false keeps the API off the gateway until deliberately exposed.
